The difference between the purchase price and the fair </span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:117pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">value of the net assets acquired (including identifiable intangible assets) is recorded as goodwill or bargain purchase gain. </span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:129pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">Management uses significant estimates and assumptions to value such items, including projected cash flows, repayment </span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:141pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">rates, default rates and losses assuming default, discount rates, and realizable collateral values. style="display:inline-block;height:6.77pt;width:28.14pt"></span></span><span style="left:130.5pt;position:var(--position)">QUANTITATIVE AND QUALITATIVE DISCLOSURES ABOUT MARKET RISK </span></span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:69pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:bold;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">Market Risk Management</span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:93pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', forward-looking quantitative and qualitative information </span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:105pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Market risk is defined as the sensitivity of income, fair value measurements </span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:117pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">and capital to changes in interest rates, foreign currency exchange rates, commodity prices and other relevant market rates </span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:129pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">or prices. The primary market risks that we are exposed to are price and interest rate risks. Price risk is defined as the risk </span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:141pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">to current or anticipated earnings or capital arising from changes in the value of either assets or liabilities that are entered </span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:153pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">into as part of distributing or managing risk. Interest rate risk is defined as risk to current or anticipated earnings or capital </span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:165pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">arising from movements in interest rates. This forward-looking information provides an indicator of how we view and </span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:177pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">manage our ongoing market risk exposures.</span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:201pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">Mechanics is engaged primarily in the business of investing funds obtained from deposits and borrowings in interest </span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:213pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">earning loans and investments, and our primary component of market risk is sensitivity to changes in interest rates. </span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:225pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">Consequently, our earnings depend to a significant extent on our net interest income, which is the difference between </span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:237pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">interest income on loans and investments and our interest expense on deposits and borrowings. To the extent that our </span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:249pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">interest-bearing liabilities do not reprice or mature at the same time as our interest-bearing assets, we are subject to interest </span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:261pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">rate risk and corresponding fluctuations in net interest income.</span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:285pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">For the Company, price and interest rate risks arise from the financial instruments and positions we hold. This includes </span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:297pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">loans, MSRs, investment securities, deposits, borrowings, long-term debt and derivative financial instruments. Due to the </span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:309pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">nature of our current operations, we are not subject to foreign currency exchange or commodity price risk. Our real estate </span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:321pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">loan portfolio is subject to risks associated with the local economies of our various markets, in particular, the regional </span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:333pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">economy of the western United States, including Hawaii.</span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:357pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">The spread between the yield on interest-earning assets and the cost of interest-bearing liabilities and the relative dollar </span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:369pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">amounts of these assets and liabilities are the principal items affecting net interest income. Changes in net interest rates </span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:381pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">(interest rate risk) are influenced to a significant degree by the repricing characteristics of assets and liabilities (repricing </span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:393pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">risk), the relationship between various rates (basis risk), customer options (optionality risk) and changes in the shape of the </span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:405pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">yield curve (yield curve risk). We manage the available-for-sale investment securities portfolio while maintaining a balance </span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:417pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">between risk and return. The Company's funding strategy is to grow core deposits while we efficiently supplement using </span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:429pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">wholesale borrowings.</span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:453pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">We estimate the sensitivity of our net interest income to changes in market interest rates using an interest rate simulation </span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:465pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">model that includes assumptions related to the level of balance sheet growth, deposit repricing characteristics and the rate </span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:477pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">of prepayments for multiple interest rate change scenarios. Interest rate sensitivity depends on certain repricing </span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:489pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">characteristics in our interest-earnings assets and interest-bearing liabilities, including the maturity structure of assets and </span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:501pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">liabilities and their repricing characteristics during the periods of changes in market interest rates. Effective interest rate </span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:513pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">risk management seeks to ensure both assets and liabilities respond to changes in interest rates within an acceptable </span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:525pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">timeframe, minimizing the impact of interest rate changes on net interest income and capital. Interest rate sensitivity is </span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:537pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', is defined as the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an </span></ix:continuation></div><ix:continuation id="f-462-3" continuedAt="f-462-4"><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:285pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date. A fair value measurement assumes that the </span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:297pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">transaction to sell the asset or transfer the liability occurs in the principal market for the asset or liability or, in the absence </span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:309pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">of a principal market, the most advantageous market for the asset or liability. The Company&#8217;s approach is to maximize the </span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:321pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">use of observable inputs and minimize the use of unobservable inputs when developing fair value measurements.</span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:345pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:underline;white-space:pre">Fair Value Hierarchy</span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:369pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">A three-level valuation hierarchy has been established under ASC 820 for disclosure of fair value measurements. The </span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:381pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">valuation hierarchy is based on the observability of inputs to the valuation of an asset or liability as of the measurement </span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:393pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">date. A financial instrument&#8217;s categorization within the valuation hierarchy is based on the lowest level of input that is </span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:405pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">significant to the fair value measurement. The levels are defined as follows:</span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:429pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:76.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">&#8226;</span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:94.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">Level 1 &#8211; Quoted prices (unadjusted) in active markets for identical assets or liabilities that the reporting entity </span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:441pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:94.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">can access at the measurement date. An active market for the asset or liability is a market in which transactions for </span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:453pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:94.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">the asset or liability take place with sufficient frequency and volume to provide pricing information on an ongoing </span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:465pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:94.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">basis.</span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:489pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:76.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">&#8226;</span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:94.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">Level 2 &#8211; Inputs other than quoted prices included within Level 1 that are observable for the asset or liability, </span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:501pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:94.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">either directly or indirectly. This includes quoted prices for similar assets and liabilities in active markets and </span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:513pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:94.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">inputs that are observable for the asset or liability for substantially the full term of the financial instrument.</span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:537pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:76.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">&#8226;</span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:94.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">Level 3 &#8211; Unobservable inputs for the asset or liability. These inputs reflect the Company&#8217;s assumptions of what </span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:549pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:94.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">market participants would use in pricing the asset or liability.</span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:573pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">The Company&#8217;s policy regarding transfers between levels of the fair value hierarchy is that all transfers are assumed to </span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:585pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">occur at the end of the reporting period.</span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:609pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:underline;white-space:pre">Estimation of Fair Value</span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:633pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">Fair value is based on quoted market prices, when available. In cases where a quoted price for an asset or liability is not </span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:645pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">available, the Company uses valuation models to estimate fair value. These models incorporate inputs such as forward </span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:657pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">yield curves, loan prepayment assumptions, expected loss assumptions, market volatilities and pricing spreads utilizing </span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:669pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">market-based inputs where readily available. The Company believes its valuation methods are appropriate and consistent </span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:681pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">with those that would be used by other market participants. However, imprecision in estimating unobservable inputs and </span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:693pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">other factors may result in these fair value measurements The significance of the fall-out factor to the fair value </span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:494.75pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">measurement of an individual IRLC is generally highest at the time that the rate lock is initiated and declines as closing </span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:506.75pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">procedures are performed and the underlying loan gets closer to funding. The fall-out factor applied is based on historical </span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:518.75pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">experience. The value of servicing is impacted by a variety of factors, including prepayment assumptions, discount rates, </span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:530.75pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">delinquency rates, contractually specified servicing fees, servicing costs and underlying portfolio characteristics. Because </span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:542.75pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">these inputs are not observable in market trades, the fall-out factor and value of servicing are considered to be Level 3 </span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:554.75pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">inputs. The fair value of IRLCs decreases in value upon an increase in the fall-out factor and increases in value upon an </span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:566.75pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">increase in the value of servicing. Changes in the fall-out factor and value of servicing do not increase or decrease based on </span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:578.75pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">movements in other significant unobservable inputs.</span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:602.75pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">The Company recognizes unrealized gains and losses from the time that an IRLC is initiated until the gain or loss is </span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:614.75pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">realized at the time the loan closes, which generally occurs within </span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:324.23pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">30</span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:334.23pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">-</span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:337.56pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">90 days</span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:368.38pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">. For IRLCs that fall out, any unrealized gain </span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:626.75pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:58.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre">or loss is reversed, which generally occurs at the end of the commitment period. The gains and losses recognized on IRLC </span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:638.75pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', interest rate lock commitments made during the reporting period </span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:650.75pt;width:612pt"><span estimated fallout) while the amount of unrealized gains and losses realized at settlement generally </span></div><div
